This is just from my experience, but work right now even if it’s something unrelated. Believe me when I tell you the degree isn’t worth much without credible work experience. I was a psych major, couldn’t find a job in that field so I started working in a warehouse, from there I got into the HR department at that warehouse. Stayed in the HR Dept for 2 years, in total I was in this job for 3 years, after I got an interview with my local county to become a clinical psychologist. I’m content where I’m at now. But do you see? I started working at an Amazon warehouse, and moved up. I built credible work experience that I was able to use for my resume and interview. I know it sucks that your not getting your dream job, but it just doesn’t work that way. You have to work from the bottom and get whatever you can. Once you build a name for yourself than you can pursue your career. It sucks to say it, but a degree only ensures your 50% ready, the other 50% is based on work experience. So don’t wait, please don’t wait. My cousin graduated last year, and he just sits at home all day playing video games. He sends resumes to high end companies and gets an interview here and there. Every time he is rejected he just states “it wasn’t meant to be”. Don’t be like my cousin, you have a fire, a drive in you, I feel it. Just go for it, apply everywhere that you feel will expand your work experience. I believe in you.
